title: This Ant's Jaws Snap Shut at 145 Miles an Hour

scenes.text: This ant's jaws snap shut at 145 miles an hour.
The trap-jaw ant. Its mouth closes in a tenth of a millisecond. Hundreds of times faster than a blink.
The jaws hit 100,000 G. In 2006 that was the fastest strike ever measured on any animal.
Second trick: aim the jaws at the ground, fire, and the ant launches itself 8 centimetres straight up.
It catapults itself out of danger, backwards, with its own face.
Hundred and forty five miles an hour. From an ant.

description:
The trap-jaw ant Odontomachus bauri closes its mandibles at up to 145 miles an hour, in about a tenth of a millisecond.
Researchers at UC Berkeley filmed the strike with high-speed cameras in 2006 and measured accelerations of around 100,000 G, the fastest animal strike recorded at the time. By firing its jaws against the ground, the ant can also catapult itself about 8 centimetres into the air to escape predators.
Which insect superpower would you take? Comment below.
first_comment: The jaws are held open by a latch and loaded like a spring, so the power comes from stored energy, not muscle speed. What else in nature do you think works like a catapult?
